name: Build Your Own Strategy
tagline: Stop calling pre-built functions — write one.
narrative: The Snake Corridor winds back and forth across an 11×11 grid. Earlier challenges gave you pre-built functions to call. This one does not. The engine still provides the four primitives — MoveForward, TurnLeft, TurnRight, Wait — but it is up to you to compose them into strategies. A wall-following algorithm needs a specific sequence: check if the left is open, turn left if so, step forward, check again. That is not a single primitive. It is a function you author from primitives. This is the moment the platform stops giving you tools and asks you to build them.
objective: Solve the 11x11 Snake Corridor with a custom wall-following function, then hold on the goal for 3 ticks.
learningObjective: Composing reusable multi-step functions from engine primitives. Understanding that abstraction — naming a sequence of steps — is what allows brains to stay readable as they grow.
intelligenceExplanation: This brain starts with only the four engine primitives wrapped as single-step bricks. There are no pre-built strategies. The Functions tab is now unlocked — you can open it and compose new functions by sequencing primitives together. Once you have created a function like `follow-wall`, you can assign it to a rule just like any other brick. The robot will then execute that sequence, one action per tick, as a committed behavior. Arriving is not enough: the robot must stay on the goal tile for 3 consecutive ticks to confirm the arrival, so add a top-priority rule WHEN atGoal -> DO hold.
hint: Try composing a `follow-left-wall` function with steps: [pivot-left, step]. Then write a rule: when `!wallLeft`, do `follow-left-wall`. Add a fallback: when `wallAhead`, do `pivot-right`. Add a high-priority rule: when `goalAhead`, do `step`.
hints: You have the four primitives but no strategy. Open the Functions tab and compose one.
A left-hand wall follower repeats: if you can turn left, do; else go straight; else turn right.
Compose a multi-step brick from pivot-left / step / pivot-right, then call it from a single rule.

goals.description: Reach the exit of the snake corridor.

functions.description: Engine primitive: move one tile forward.
Engine primitive: do nothing this tick.
